turn_text: Welcome to another episode of Think Arctic, a podcast powered by GCI that tackles the issues facing the Arctic and its stakeholders. Thank you for joining us. I'm your host, Holly Nolan. Let's start by talking about what you feel are priorities in the Arctic.

I would say that there's not one priority. There's numerous priorities. One, I would like to see navigational aids put in for the transit vessels that are international vessels that's not there now. Establishing through the Maritime Association Organization, universally, channels. I like to see a communication system put in where everybody's immediate contact with all types of activities. And of course, I want to build a port.
With the Arctic opening up, what opportunities do you see?

Well, again, we don't have any facilities up there of any consequence. We need to build a port that can take deep draft vessels. We need a Coast Guard station in the Arctic. We have a great one in Kodiak, but we need an Arctic Coast Guard station. And we need to get, I would say, some of the newer cutters built up there, and plus the ice breakers, which we hope to get.
What kind of success have you seen in the Arctic over the last few years?

the success I see is of anything. It's, of course, the mineral exploration and the oil exploration has been successful and we have not developed. But we know the potential there. And to some people that's not good, but to the nations and whole, that's very good. It's not the fuel that we're pumping now. We drill through three different layers of oil to get to what we call the premium oil, a high quality oil. But all above that are different velocities of the oil that we learn more. We'll be able to extract that for this nation.
